summary: This two-line program prints the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, each on its own line. It uses a for loop with range() to walk through a sequence of numbers instead of writing five separate print statements.

lines.text: range(1, 6) produces the numbers starting at 1 and stopping just before 6, so the loop runs five times. The end value is not included, which is why counting to 5 needs a 6 here — this is the single most common off-by-one mistake beginners make.
The variable i is the loop variable: on each pass through the loop Python assigns it the next number in the range, so its value changes automatically without you writing i = i + 1.

The indentation is what puts this line inside the loop body, so it is what gets repeated. Remove the indentation and Python would report an error, because a for statement must be followed by an indented block.
